FaultIsolation.Title: Error isolation - C08
FaultIsolation.Description: Always active. If a COMET module fails, release its controls and let SAIN take over. Other bots continue normally. Repeated failures disable that module for the affected bot until the raid ends. Failed cleanup or state recovery disables COMET for that bot. Retries use fresh bot state and still require the usual eligibility checks. The window must be at least as long as the retry delay. Diagnostics and RR show the affected module, cause and recovery state.

CoverScan.Title: Stable cover search - C07
CoverScan.Description: Keep the last complete list of covers while SAIN searches for replacements. Check a cover again before moving to it. A completed empty search clears the old results. This limits a single search, not the lifetime of a valid cover. Changing enemy or entering Ghost clears the old context. Only the AI host runs this feature.
CoverScan.Summary: Keep the last complete list of covers while SAIN searches for replacements.

MovementRecovery.Title: Stuck movement recovery - C06
MovementRecovery.Description: Help awake PMCs that are trying to move but stay in place, including SAIN and ORBIT movement. Medical actions, reloading, door animations and intentional waits keep priority. Only real movement confirms recovery. Stages must stay in increasing order. Relocation is limited to a clear walkable route, at most 2 m, hidden from every player and at least 50 m away. Each stage is tried once per blockage. In Fika, only the AI host acts.
MovementRecovery.Summary: Help awake PMCs that are trying to move but stay in place, including SAIN and ORBIT movement.

DoorClosing.Title: Automatic door closing - C05
DoorClosing.Description: Off by default: PMCs leave open doors alone while moving. Enable only to close a blocking leaf when the closed door would leave their route clear. Tactical closes and player interactions are separate. The whole swing must be clear. Tactical reservations and reversed-leaf recovery take priority.
DoorClosing.Summary: Off by default: PMCs leave open doors alone while moving.

DoorMotion.Title: Push doors away and clear blocked leaves - C04
DoorMotion.Description: Push doors away from PMCs. If an inverted leaf traps a moving PMC, swing it back gradually after checking the space and nearby players.

DoorSpatial.Title: Door frames and panels - C03
DoorSpatial.Description: Keep tactical positions clear of the actual door panels, including partly open and neighbouring doors. Native and Waypoints frames use the same geometry. Uncertain positions are rejected.
DoorSpatial.Summary: Keep tactical positions clear of the actual door panels, including partly open and neighbouring doors.

DoorRecovery.Title: Recover stalled doors - C02
DoorRecovery.Description: Finish frozen door interactions on PMC routes, including stalled animations. Correct the angle and interaction record so the door can be used again. Active players, reserved doors and locks keep priority. One repair attempt per interaction, with collision checks. In Fika, COMET synchronizes corrections from the host.
DoorRecovery.Summary: Finish frozen door interactions on PMC routes, including stalled animations.

DoorTransit.Title: Door traversal - C01
DoorTransit.Description: During PMC movement, including SAIN combat paths, bots anticipate doors on their route and slow down only for an obstructed passage. Clear openings do not slow an escape. A blocked bot can retry the native interaction, then reconsider its route. Door interactions and occupied doors pause the blockage timer. Tactical door maneuvers keep their own rules.
DoorTransit.Summary: During PMC movement, including SAIN combat paths, bots anticipate doors on their route and slow down only for an obstructed passage.

Outcomes.Title: Tactical feedback - E04
Outcomes.Description: PMCs remember the observed results of their own actions during this encounter. Two comparable results can slightly influence a later choice. Reaching a position or hitting an enemy alone does not count as success. Ambiguous outcomes are neutral; urgent decisions still take priority. Memory is individual and cleared when the encounter ends. No knowledge is carried between raids.
Outcomes.Summary: PMCs remember the observed results of their own actions during this encounter.

Encounter.Title: Repeated peeks - E03
Encounter.Description: A PMC can favor watching an opening after personally seeing the same opponent reappear there several times during this fight. This is a preference, not a guaranteed reaction. Nothing is learned from previous raids or shared automatically with squadmates. Continuous visibility counts once. A nearby obstacle and a stable viewpoint are required. Native contact expiry and combat priorities always apply; memory cannot reveal a hidden position.
Encounter.Summary: A PMC can favor watching an opening after personally seeing the same opponent reappear there several times during this fight.

RestLights.Title: Lights while resting - L03
RestLights.Description: Switch off weapon lamps and lasers when a PMC settles into a quiet wait or camp outside combat. ORBIT camps are supported when ORBIT is installed; ordinary game idle waits also work. One attempt per pause, preserving each accessory's mode. Looting, busy hands, known threats and Ghost Mode are excluded. If another system changes a device, COMET yields for that pause. SAIN decides when to turn lights back on.
RestLights.Summary: Switch off weapon lamps and lasers when a PMC settles into a quiet wait or camp outside combat.

TacticalDevices.Title: Weapon lights and lasers - L02
TacticalDevices.Description: Apply SAIN's lighting choice to every accessory on the held weapon. Keep each selected mode, including IR, and retry failed accessories without repeated clicking. Ambush concealment keeps priority. Busy hands wait without consuming attempts. A laser or IR accessory counts as active even without visible light. Accessories are also switched off when a ready weapon is put away, using its normal game command.
TacticalDevices.Summary: Apply SAIN's lighting choice to every accessory on the held weapon.

LightDiscipline.Title: Lights during an ambush - L01
LightDiscipline.Description: PMCs switch off their weapon lights and lasers while holding an angle on a hidden enemy. SAIN regains lighting control when the enemy becomes visible or the bot starts another action. Device modes, including IR, are preserved; COMET never forces a light ON. Uses personal sight or hearing, never the hidden enemy's actual position. Moving slowly by itself is not an ambush. If another system changes an accessory, it keeps control for that wait.
LightDiscipline.Summary: PMCs switch off their weapon lights and lasers while holding an angle on a hidden enemy.

SquadVoice.Title: Squad voice - S09
SquadVoice.Description: Enable or mute PMC squad callouts, as in zzap. Pain, death, taunts and independent voices are unchanged.
SquadVoice.Summary: Keep normal SAIN callouts, reduce them, or mute squad communication.

SquadFire.Title: Protect your squad while firing - S08
SquadFire.Description: PMCs stop firing when a living squadmate crosses their barrel or is about to cross it. Once the lane stays clear, SAIN decides whether to shoot again. Other groups are not covered by S08; native safety checks still apply. Bullets already fired cannot be stopped. Every new trigger request is checked immediately. Doors and glass do not hide squadmates from this check. If cover is uncertain, the bot protects its squadmate.
SquadFire.Summary: PMCs stop firing when a living squadmate crosses their barrel or is about to cross it.

FireLane.Title: Avoid allied firing lanes - S07
FireLane.Description: PMCs briefly yield to a squadmate who is actually firing, or step out through a checked opening. Direct combat and escape keep priority. If no safe detour exists, native movement resumes after the short wait. This does not stop the shooter's weapon.
FireLane.Summary: PMCs briefly yield to a squadmate who is actually firing, or step out through a checked opening.

SquadStorm.Title: Rush a vulnerable enemy together - S06
SquadStorm.Description: Nearby PMCs can approach together using observed equipment or personally heard openings. At least two willing attackers need a safe route and must be ready before departure. Unknown gear is neutral. Grenades and urgent threats cancel the plan; native combat resumes when the enemy is visible. Others keep their own action. Uses the observation limits from A09 and the estimated sound windows from A10, even when their individual score bonuses are disabled. A retry also requires newer evidence.
SquadStorm.Summary: Let nearby, willing squadmates coordinate a push against a vulnerable known opponent.

SquadTrade.Title: React to a teammate death - S05
SquadTrade.Description: A PMC who witnesses a confirmed squadmate death can approach a known attacker or watch a protected angle. A missing, extracted or downed teammate does not trigger this. Unknown killers only allow sector watching, using information the PMC already has. One independent choice per PMC and death. Several squadmates may react from different positions. Fear, injuries, loaded ammunition and safe routes still matter. A failed push falls back to watching; visible enemies and urgent actions return control to SAIN. Aggressive uses the current SAIN personality's rush trait. Watching ends at its configured time limit; it never fires at an unseen enemy.
SquadTrade.Summary: A PMC who witnesses a confirmed squadmate death can approach a known attacker or watch a protected angle.

MedicalChoice.Title: Choose the right treatment - H01
MedicalChoice.Description: Choose first aid, a useful stim, surgery or waiting. Urgent bleeding and vital injuries come first. Long treatments need reached, protective cover when threats are known. Native medicines, animations and resources are preserved. Surgery requires enough time without new information and enough distance from known threats, as configured below. A selected treatment is rechecked before starting; ongoing treatment is not replaced by another score. Emergency bleeding treatment can start without perfect cover.
MedicalChoice.Summary: Prioritize urgent injuries and seek suitable cover for longer treatments.

SurgeryInterruption.Title: Interrupt unsafe surgery - H02
SurgeryInterruption.Description: Stop an ongoing H01 surgery when danger gets too close. A new hit or detected dangerous grenade requests an immediate native cancellation. The PMC still needs time to put away the kit and ready a weapon. Uses only threats the PMC has seen or heard. The distance and age limits below determine which contacts are close enough to interrupt. After interruption, wait for the configured retry delay and satisfy medical safety checks again. First aid stays available. Requires H01; native medicine costs and animations are unchanged.
SurgeryInterruption.Summary: Stop surgery when the PMC detects a nearby threat; normal cancellation animations still apply.

CoverMate.Title: Cover a busy teammate - S04
CoverMate.Description: Watch a useful protected angle while a nearby PMC actually reloads or uses medicine. Keep a suitable current position, or take a short checked route. Extra protectors need different sectors. Visible combat and urgent actions retain priority.
CoverMate.Summary: Watch a useful protected angle while a nearby PMC actually reloads or uses medicine.

SquadManeuver.Title: Coordinate support and flanking - S03
SquadManeuver.Description: When an enemy hides, squadmates can hold an angle while others find different approaches. Several PMCs may flank together, with at least one confirmed supporter. Uses S01 movement and S02 entrances; their angle, route and participation settings still apply.
SquadManeuver.Summary: Some squadmates hold the angle while others look for another approach.

SecondaryEntrance.Title: Watch another access, then consider entering - S02
SecondaryEntrance.Description: A teammate can watch a different entrance while the squad keeps the enemy busy. Uses S01's participation roll. Several teammates may choose different accesses. Entry needs a ready partner and recent information. The entry chance is rolled once per attempt. The retry also requires newer information. A blocked passage or unavailable partner never forces an entry.
SecondaryEntrance.Summary: A teammate can watch a different entrance while the squad keeps the enemy busy.

Crossfire.Title: Find another firing angle - S01
Crossfire.Description: When a teammate is engaging a known enemy, each PMC can choose a different reachable angle. Several teammates may move at once if their positions and routes are useful. No one is forced to move. Visible enemies, healing and immediate dangers keep priority. Uses only remembered or shared contact information. Positions are spaced apart, firing lanes are checked, and failed routes are abandoned. Indoor angle must not exceed outdoor angle; stall timeout must not exceed movement timeout. Settings apply next raid.
Crossfire.Summary: When a teammate is engaging a known enemy, each PMC can choose a different reachable angle.

ReadyStance.Title: Keep the weapon ready after a fight - H05
ReadyStance.Description: Keep the gun raised briefly after a real fight. Nearby fresh threats extend the window. This does not force ADS or change combat, objectives or Ghost eligibility. Medicine, reloads, sprinting and interactions keep priority. The nearby duration must be at least the normal duration. Old clues cannot keep restarting the timer. Settings apply next raid.
ReadyStance.Summary: Keep the gun raised briefly after a real fight.

MedicalPosture.Title: Keep the body in during treatment - H03
MedicalPosture.Description: Stop leaning and pause COMET peeks, combat steps and new jumps while healing, using a stim or performing surgery. Also protects native SAIN treatment, including Bot Healing Fixes.
MedicalPosture.Summary: Stop leaning and pause COMET peeks, combat steps and new jumps while healing, using a stim or performing surgery.

ExplosionAwareness.Title: React to nearby explosions - G10
ExplosionAwareness.Description: A nearby explosion can register its thrower as an enemy. SAIN then reports the thrower's position with its native distance-based dispersion and squad sharing. Already known throwers keep native explosion handling. No separate look lock or witnessed-throw requirement.
ExplosionAwareness.Summary: A nearby explosion can register its thrower as an enemy.

FlashContinuity.Title: Preserve ongoing flash effects - G09
FlashContinuity.Description: Real flashbangs keep SAIN's normal duration, live enemy memory and recovery stages. Continuous gas can refresh ongoing blindness without repeating the initial flash side effects or fixed stat modifiers. Durations and strength for real flashes come from your SAIN preset.
FlashContinuity.Summary: Real flashbangs keep SAIN's normal duration, live enemy memory and recovery stages.

GasExposure.Title: CS gas reactions - G08
GasExposure.Description: Requires Manimal-CSGas 2.0.0 or 2.0.1 on the AI host. Supports CS, RDA-68 and RDA-78 using their actual cloud shape and protection rules. Bots first scatter from the canister for five seconds, then build irritation. Sufficient exposure refreshes blindness; there is no extra custom escape path. Ordinary smoke is unchanged.
GasExposure.Summary: Requires Manimal-CSGas 2.0.0 or 2.0.1 on the AI host.

GrenadeFilter.Title: Offensive grenade types - G07
GrenadeFilter.Description: Use fragmentation and flash grenades for attacks. Smoke, gas, persistent and unknown effects are excluded. An excluded item can be replaced by a suitable grenade the PMC actually carries. With G03 enabled, a safe flash is a fallback when no suitable timed fragmentation grenade is available. Flash fuses keep the arrival safety margin without the fragmentation minimum fuse. Native permissions, hands and throw safety still apply. Defensive smoke use is a separate future tactic.
GrenadeFilter.Summary: Choose which grenade types PMCs may use offensively.

GrenadeDispersion.Title: Squad grenade dispersion - G06
GrenadeDispersion.Description: Squadmates escaping a grenade prefer separate safe destinations. In a narrow exit, safety comes first: nobody waits for a free spot. Requires Grenade reactions (G05). Only nearby awake PMCs in the same squad who are already escaping take part. A safe destination stays stable; this does not give other bots knowledge of the grenade.
GrenadeDispersion.Summary: Squadmates escaping a grenade prefer separate safe destinations.

GrenadeReaction.Title: Grenade reactions - G05
GrenadeReaction.Description: PMCs use SAIN's grenade detection and reaction delay. Personality influences the escape, but every destination and route must be safe. Solid walls may protect a bot; glass and doors are not trusted. Distances are search preferences, adapted to reachable terrain. A destination is kept only while safe. Prone is a last resort after the search finds no safe escape.
GrenadeReaction.Summary: PMCs use SAIN's grenade detection and reaction delay.

OwnGrenadeSafety.Title: Own grenade safety - G04
OwnGrenadeSafety.Description: Track real grenades after throwing. Keep PMCs and nearby squadmates who saw the throw away from unsafe routes. A rebound cancels the assault and asks SAIN to escape. A missing projectile is not a confirmed explosion. Departure grace only applies while the grenade moves away. Solid cover may protect a waiting PMC; doors and glass are not treated as guaranteed cover. Room entry keeps its existing pause after a confirmed explosion.

GrenadeChoice.Title: Choose a grenade - G03
GrenadeChoice.Description: Choose from carried timed fragmentation grenades: shorter fuse indoors or nearby, longer fuse outdoors at range. Keep a safety margin after estimated arrival. Native throwing and SAIN permission checks still apply. Flight time is an estimate from the native trajectory. Impact grenades, smoke and flash grenades are outside this feature. Selection is not a confirmed throw; RR tracks those separately.
GrenadeChoice.Summary: Choose from carried timed fragmentation grenades: shorter fuse indoors or nearby, longer fuse outdoors at range.

GrenadeTrajectory.Title: Find a grenade trajectory - G02
GrenadeTrajectory.Description: Aim at the last personally known position, a nearby corner or behind an open door. Prefer throws with more clearance around obstacles. SAIN still handles throwing and the game's grenade physics. Failed searches use G01's "Retry without a trajectory" setting, even with grenade judgment disabled. Random aiming error is kept for the whole attempt. The door, trajectory and nearby nonhostiles are checked again before throwing.
GrenadeTrajectory.Summary: Aim at the last personally known position, a nearby corner or behind an open door.

GrenadeJudgment.Title: Choose when to throw a grenade - G01
GrenadeJudgment.Description: Spend a real grenade only when a safe SAIN trajectory and recent personal contact make it worthwhile. One shared roll is used by SAIN and COMET's combat, room entry and relocation decisions. Bonuses cannot bypass safety. A stale position is not proof of camping. SAIN's grenade permissions and cooldown still apply. While G01 is enabled, it replaces the extra grenade preference roll in room entry. RR records the reason, chance, roll, native acceptance and actual projectile release separately.
GrenadeJudgment.Summary: Adjust the starting chance to throw a real grenade when contact and trajectory checks allow it.

HandsRecovery.Title: Recover stuck hands - W10
HandsRecovery.Description: Recover stale reload or weapon-switch flags, or a grenade left in hand after cancellation. Real reloads, medicine, weapon changes and intentional grenade actions are allowed to finish. A stale switch is cleared only when the held weapon and inventory agree. A missing reload completion notification can be retried after at least 16 seconds with the magazine inserted and the animation already idle. Recovery never creates ammunition or fast-forwards animations. RR distinguishes a request from an observed recovery.
HandsRecovery.Summary: Recover confirmed stuck hands without interrupting real weapon operations.

RecoilRecovery.Title: Recover from DMR and sniper recoil faster - W09
RecoilRecovery.Description: Optional difficulty adjustment: return the aim towards its pre-shot direction faster between shots. Initial recoil stays with SAIN. Higher values improve follow-up precision, without changing fire rate or initial recoil. Logs and RR show observed aim offsets before and after recovery, not guaranteed hits.
RecoilRecovery.Summary: Optional difficulty adjustment: return the aim towards its pre-shot direction faster between shots.

ShotGeometry.Title: Avoid wasted shots into obstacles - W08
ShotGeometry.Description: Check the path from the muzzle before unseen-target fire, including corner prefire, suppression and blind fire. Doors and window glass always allow an attempt, even with penetration estimates disabled. Other obstacles and allies still block the shot. Native ballistics decide what the bullet actually penetrates. Allies and permitted paths are checked each frame; only static blocked paths can use the longer cache. Visible-target shooting stays with SAIN.
ShotGeometry.Summary: Check the path from the muzzle before unseen-target fire, including corner prefire, suppression and blind fire.

SuppressionDiscipline.Title: Use short suppression bursts - W07
SuppressionDiscipline.Description: Keep pressure on a recently seen or personally located attacker, while saving ammunition for their next peek. Pauses vary by ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â±30%. A visible target immediately gets normal SAIN fire. The native fire mode and cadence stay unchanged; corner prefire keeps its own rules. SAIN's suppression toggles still apply.
SuppressionDiscipline.Summary: Keep pressure on a recently seen or personally located attacker, while saving ammunition for their next peek.

WeaponSync.Title: Keep weapon information up to date - W06
WeaponSync.Description: After a PMC loots, replaces or modifies a weapon, keep its weapon selection and reload information in sync with its real equipment. Equipment changes trigger a check automatically. The backup checks the three weapon slots. Ongoing reloads and other hands operations are allowed to finish. No ammunition is added and no weapon change is forced.
WeaponSync.Summary: After a PMC loots, replaces or modifies a weapon, keep its weapon selection and reload information in sync with its real equipment.

WeaponRange.Title: Choose a weapon for the distance - W05
WeaponRange.Description: Compare both primary weapons using their actual sights, firing modes and ammunition. Keep the current weapon when the benefit is small or uncertain. A nearby known threat takes priority over a distant target. Between the two distances, keep the current choice. Hearing alone cannot trigger a long-range switch. Reloads, healing, grenades and firing take priority. The minimum hold and refusal delay from W03 also apply to W05, even if automatic returns are disabled. RR shows the comparison and confirms when the new weapon is actually ready.
WeaponRange.Summary: Compare both primary weapons using their actual sights, firing modes and ammunition.

QuickReload.Title: Emergency fast reload - W04
QuickReload.Description: Under immediate pressure, PMCs with low ammo can drop their magazine for a native fast reload. The dropped magazine and its remaining rounds stay in the world. Only accessible, compatible, loaded spares count. The replacement counts towards the minimum, so a minimum of two leaves at least one spare. It must contain more rounds than the current magazine. Protective cover favors a normal reload unless the PMC is taking fire. W01 chooses when to reload and W02 can choose the pistol first. Native animation speed is unchanged. RR distinguishes the request, animation, actual magazine drop and completion.
QuickReload.Summary: Under immediate pressure, PMCs with low ammo can drop their magazine for a native fast reload.

WeaponReturn.Title: Return to the primary weapon - W03
WeaponReturn.Description: PMCs keep a useful weapon instead of repeatedly switching back and forth. They return from the pistol when the threat moves away or things calm down, and give the primary time to reload. Holding time starts when the weapon is ready in hand. Urgent switches to a loaded weapon remain possible. Reloads and native animations are allowed to finish. An empty primary without usable reserves is not a valid return target.
WeaponReturn.Summary: PMCs keep a useful weapon instead of repeatedly switching back and forth.

PistolSwap.Title: Draw a pistol under pressure - W02
PistolSwap.Description: With a close known threat and an empty or nearly empty primary, PMCs can draw a loaded pistol instead of reloading. Safe cover can still make reloading the better choice. Both ammo limits must be met. The pistol must have more loaded rounds than the primary, including chambers. Existing reloads and native draw animations are respected. RR distinguishes an accepted request, the pistol in hand and readiness.
PistolSwap.Summary: With a close known threat and an empty or nearly empty primary, PMCs can draw a loaded pistol instead of reloading.

ReloadTiming.Title: Choose when to reload - W01
ReloadTiming.Description: PMCs weigh remaining ammo against cover and known threats. A lost contact is not automatically safe. Ammo in the chamber counts, and a replacement magazine must contain more rounds. Critical priority also depends on the weapon: a few shells are not the same as a few rounds in an automatic weapon. Urgent changes override stability. Native animations and weapon fallbacks stay with SAIN.
ReloadTiming.Summary: PMCs weigh remaining ammo against cover and known threats.

CoverFeint.Title: Feint from cover - M14
CoverFeint.Description: PMCs outdoors can briefly show themselves and return behind cover, or check their magazine to invite an approach. Enemies remain free to react normally. A magazine check is not a reload. Bait peeks require a healthy, aggressive PMC and a safe return route. Exposure starts only after actual arrival. The magazine hold starts only once the animation ends and the weapon is ready. A retry also needs fresh incoming fire, a new personal sound or a meaningful change in the known contact position. RR separates requests, observed movement, native sound playback and observed enemy reactions.
CoverFeint.Summary: Briefly expose a PMC to invite a shot, then return to cover.

OutdoorRelocation.Title: Change cover after contact - M13
OutdoorRelocation.Description: Once safe behind cover, a PMC may change position instead of showing up at the same angle. The new cover and its route must be worthwhile. Injuries, observed enemy weapons, personality and squad support adjust the base chance. Another attempt needs both the delay and new incoming fire or a meaningful change in the known enemy position. The angle is a preference, not a mandatory minimum. Urgent native actions keep priority.
OutdoorRelocation.Summary: Once safe behind cover, a PMC may change position instead of showing up at the same angle.

TacticalJump.Title: Tactical jumps and firing in the air - M12
TacticalJump.Description: Door peeks, corner moves and evasive retreats share one flight check. Jumps need real momentum and a clear route. Unstuck jumps and vaulting keep their own rules. Each PMC rolls once per opponent for permission to fire in the air. Other PMCs hold fire until they land. Permission still requires SAIN's normal aiming and shooting checks. Existing speed and stamina limits for each tactic still apply. Extra stamina at 0 keeps those limits. Disabling this section restores each tactic's previous jump behavior.
TacticalJump.Summary: Allow firing during an otherwise eligible tactical jump, subject to normal aiming checks.

RetreatWeave.Title: Evade while sprinting to cover - M11
RetreatWeave.Description: PMCs fleeing a personally perceived threat behind them can zigzag, lower their head and mix in running jumps. This can continue until cover is reached. SAIN keeps the route, movement speed and physics. Intermediate jumps stop within 6 m of cover; the arrival jump gets one roll at 3-5 m. The bot runs straight while airborne. Obstacles, uncertain landings, firing and lost progress take priority. RR separates requests, accepted jumps, observed takeoff and landing.
RetreatWeave.Summary: PMCs fleeing a personally perceived threat behind them can zigzag, lower their head and mix in running jumps.

AdsTravel.Title: Release ADS while moving to safety - M10
AdsTravel.Description: PMCs can leave their sights to move freely toward cover or during a retreat, escape or push. SAIN keeps its route, movement speed and shooting. M09 can still keep the weapon facing the threat. Firing or preparing a shot immediately returns ADS to SAIN, including between bursts. Arriving, stopping or changing actions also releases the override. RR distinguishes SAIN's wish, the release request and observed ADS.
AdsTravel.Summary: PMCs can leave their sights to move freely toward cover or during a retreat, escape or push.

CoverTravel.Title: Face the threat on the way to cover - M09
CoverTravel.Description: Walk while facing a recently seen enemy, or dash along a short route to protected cover. The actual route, turns and estimated exposure guide the choice. All PMC personalities are eligible. Healing, reloading, immediate danger and other tactics keep priority. Long exposed crossings remain with SAIN. A short time limit and progress check prevent prolonged backward walking. Geometry uses a shared work budget. RR shows the chosen mode, known contact, cover destination, route exposure and actual movement separately. Only the Fika host/headless decides.
CoverTravel.Summary: Walk while facing a recently seen enemy, or dash along a short route to protected cover.

HoldAngle.Title: Open the watched angle - M08
HoldAngle.Description: A PMC waiting behind an obstacle can raise its posture or take a short step to see the approach. Both its eyes and muzzle must clear the obstruction. The safest useful candidate wins; there is no personality roll. One correction per Hold. A failed attempt needs both the retry delay and a meaningful change of position or known contact before trying again. The original Hold time limit keeps running. Medical actions, intentional cover, visible threats and door tactics keep priority.
HoldAngle.Summary: A PMC waiting behind an obstacle can raise its posture or take a short step to see the approach.

AngleWatch.Title: Watch useful angles - M07
AngleWatch.Description: Awake PMCs prepare their gaze using recent personal sightings or sounds. No random roll, firing request or movement out of cover. A sound only justifies watching. Stairs and known elevated contacts keep their useful vertical angles. Visible threats, firing, urgent actions, sight continuity, corner chase/prefire and door tactics keep priority. A blocked angle is dropped immediately at the next geometry check. After a completed preparation, the same spot cannot restart it until the bot or known contact moves 2 m. RR shows the chosen opening, evidence, alternatives and observed orientation. Host/headless only with Fika.
AngleWatch.Summary: Awake PMCs prepare their gaze using recent personal sightings or sounds.

CornerPrefire.Title: Prefire around a corner - M06
CornerPrefire.Description: Requires a walking M05 chase and a recent personal sighting near the corner. One roll per opportunity, never combined with the running jump. Sound alone cannot trigger it. The PMC aims beyond the corner and waits for its muzzle to clear the wall. It stops at the first limit, on an ally crossing the line of fire, or when SAIN needs to take over. Semi-auto is limited to one shot; native burst modes are left to SAIN. For ammunition, the stricter of rounds and percentage applies. Start limits must exceed reserves. The observation age limit applies throughout firing. M05 supplies the retry cooldown and requires a new sighting. RR records the request, native acceptance, actual shots and stop reason. Host/headless only with Fika.
CornerPrefire.Summary: Requires a walking M05 chase and a recent personal sighting near the corner.

CornerChase.Title: Chase around a corner - M05
CornerChase.Description: When a PMC is already pursuing an enemy it just saw disappear around a solid corner, it can lean into the turn, take a wider angle or try one running jump. Uncertain contacts favor a gradual approach. Hold, retreat, doors and urgent actions keep priority. One chance per loss of sight. The bot uses its last personal observation, stops the maneuver on reacquisition, and cannot retry without seeing the enemy again. These are independent chances, not a personality distribution. Jumping requires room, real momentum and stamina; otherwise the bot walks the angle. RR distinguishes requested movement from observed movement, takeoff and landing. Host/headless only with Fika.
CornerChase.Summary: When a PMC is already pursuing an enemy it just saw disappear around a solid corner, it can lean into the turn, take a wider angle or try one running jump.

CombatLean.Title: Head movement in combat - M04
CombatLean.Description: Make a PMC's head less predictable to aim at, including in the open. Works while standing or taking combat steps. SAIN keeps its normal animation speed and firing rules. Each sequence gets one chance roll and at most one short Q/E burst. Native cover leans, corner peeks, sprinting, jumps and urgent actions take priority. A firing pause keeps the current side stable.
CombatLean.Summary: Make a PMC's head less predictable to aim at, including in the open.

CornerPeek.Title: Corner peeks - M03
CornerPeek.Description: A PMC can step out, engage and return behind an angle. Requires M01. The chance is rolled after M01 selects the PMC; it is not the percentage of all PMCs. Each attempt replaces ordinary combat steps and their firing pause. Bold profiles can try one useful jump or one covered crossing. Unsafe variants fall back to a lateral step. SAIN controls firing. The firing and covered windows start only after arrival is observed; the total limit includes movement. The remaining style share is lateral movement. Jump and crossing shares apply to Chads, GigaChads and a stable half of Normals; other profiles use lateral steps.
CornerPeek.Summary: Step out from cover, engage, then return behind the angle.

FirePause.Title: Pause to fire - M02
FirePause.Description: After moving, a PMC can briefly stop to steady a shot, then move again. Requires M01. One chance is rolled per sequence, with at most one pause. SAIN still chooses when to fire. Pause time starts once the bot has actually stopped. A hit, danger, lost sight or unavailable weapon interrupts it. Pauses fit inside M01's distance and time limits. RR shows whether the stop and shots really happened.
FirePause.Summary: After moving, a PMC can briefly stop to steady a shot, then move again.

CombatStep.Title: Move while shooting - M01
CombatStep.Description: PMCs can take short lateral or diagonal steps during a firefight. They stay near their starting position, preserve cover and yield to urgent actions. A chance is rolled once per opportunity, not every frame. Shooting and movement physics remain SAIN's and the game's. These are independent chances, not a personality distribution. The distance, step timing, sequence and retry limits below bound each attempt. An unsafe route or lost sight stops movement early. RR shows the requested steps, actual distance and rejected directions. Fika decisions run only on the host/headless.
CombatStep.Summary: PMCs can take short lateral or diagonal steps during a firefight.

DoorEntry.Title: Door entry - D15
DoorEntry.Description: Enter through a usable doorway using COMET door corrections and existing movement. Squad spacing and collision checks remain active.
DoorEntry.Summary: Enter through a usable doorway using COMET door corrections and existing movement.

DoorApproach.Title: Prepare a doorway approach - D01
DoorApproach.Description: While searching for a lost contact, a PMC can move beside a nearby door before continuing. It compares both sides, checks the route and standing space, and uses only the enemy's last known position. After reaching the frame, a PMC can choose a prepared entry on recent information (D07), or a cautious check on older information (D08). Otherwise it can try a feint, reconnaissance, or continue searching. RR records the choice and the observed result.
DoorApproach.Summary: While searching for a lost contact, a PMC can move beside a nearby door before continuing.

DoorRoomClear.Title: Prepare a room entry - D07
DoorRoomClear.Description: With a recent contact behind a door, a PMC can open it from cover, optionally feint once, then enter directly or throw a real grenade first. It waits for that grenade's confirmed explosion and for its weapon to be ready. An explosion does not mean the enemy is dead. Contact age, ammunition, stamina and entry depth must meet the limits below. Grenades still respect SAIN and COMET's grenade limits. One feint uses the shared settings below. Retrying needs the opponent cooldown to expire and newer information. The plan is checked again before entering. A blocked door, unsafe throw, missing explosion or failed arrival ends the plan. RR shows the reason, alternatives, grenade evidence and actual movement.
DoorRoomClear.Summary: Prepare an entry from cover, with an optional feint or grenade before moving inside.

DoorReservation.Title: D14 - Coordinate doorway maneuvers
DoorReservation.Description: One PMC per squad prepares, peeks or enters through a door at a time. Teammates can support or choose another action. Normal movement is never blocked. Applies within each squad only. Interruptions release the door; resuming requires a new reservation. Renewal never extends the maneuver's original time limit.
DoorReservation.Summary: One PMC per squad prepares, peeks or enters through a door at a time.

DoorEmergency.Title: D13 - React when an enemy comes out
DoorEmergency.Description: Cancel a doorway feint or preparation and recover the weapon. A nearby sound is a warning, not proof that the enemy has left the room. A close visible enemy can trigger a short move to verified cover. Urgent healing, grenades and committed actions take priority. Weapon recovery uses the real animation. The cancelled plan is not resumed. RR distinguishes the warning, accepted action, actual movement and return to normal combat.
DoorEmergency.Summary: Cancel a doorway feint or preparation and recover the weapon.

DoorInterruption.Title: D12 - Interrupt and resume door plans
DoorInterruption.Description: React to a new threat first. Resume only if normal target selection returns to the original contact and the door is still safe. Original time limits keep running. Committed jumps, throws and entries are never replayed. A window of 15 seconds is a maximum, not extra time. Used feints and grenades stay consumed. Supports release their positions and must qualify again within their original limits.
DoorInterruption.Summary: React to a new threat first.

DoorSupport.Title: D11 - Door support and rear watch
DoorSupport.Description: Nearby PMC squadmates can cover a door or watch a rear approach. They must already know the same enemy. The initiator never waits for them. Combat, healing and other urgent actions take priority. One supporter covers the door; a second watches a clear rear access. Roles end with the initiator or the contact. Existing hold and plan limits can shorten this time. Each role allows one replacement, without resetting the timer.
DoorSupport.Summary: Nearby PMC squadmates can cover a door or watch a rear approach.

DoorAmbush.Title: Wait at a doorway - D09 / D10
DoorAmbush.Description: When a PMC has already chosen to hold, find a protected angle on the doorway exit. This does not make every bot camp or reveal an enemy through a closed door. Keep a good current angle. Move only for a protected doorway position with enough time left to use it. Otherwise keep a useful native Hold or reconsider another action. Feints retain D05/D06 chances, permissions and cooldowns. No forced enemy reaction. The door stays as it is. Waits begin after arrival or confirmation of the current angle, and may end earlier. Contact memory and the shared A12 hold budget still apply, including approach and feint time. The hold limit comes from Stalled plans (A12), or Lost contact (A01) when A12 is disabled. Changing doors never resets it. Danger or a visible enemy immediately returns priority to SAIN. Requires D01 doorway approach. RR distinguishes a retained position from a requested move or confirmed arrival, a clear eye/muzzle view, and an enemy actually spotted.
DoorAmbush.Summary: When a PMC has already chosen to hold, find a protected angle on the doorway exit.

DoorSearchClear.Title: Check a room while searching - D08
DoorSearchClear.Description: Allow a prepared doorway entry using remembered search contact information up to 120 seconds old. The preparation chance stays constant within that window. Uses the same clear session, grenade preparation and feint options as prepared room entries. The search variant follows the bot's current search decision, including fresh contacts; it is not selected merely by contact age. Requires doorway approach and prepared room entries.
DoorSearchClear.Summary: Allow a prepared doorway entry using remembered search contact information up to 120 seconds old.

DoorJumpPeek.Title: Doorway reconnaissance - D02 / D03
DoorJumpPeek.Description: One chance to investigate after reaching a protected frame. The PMC chooses one safe style, then resumes normal decisions. It does not chain both maneuvers. These chances apply when no feint was selected. D02 personality chances and cooldown apply to both reconnaissance styles together. For example, with Chad set to 25% and run-by preference at 40%, both routes being safe gives 10% run-by, 15% jump peek and 75% normal search.
DoorJumpPeek.Summary: Let PMCs briefly peek or run past a doorway to check a known threat.

DoorFakeMedical.Title: Doorway feints - D05 / D06
DoorFakeMedical.Description: Medical feints start a real item animation, then cancel it when the item is seen in the hands. Bleeding, serious injury and real medical decisions take priority. No item is refunded and no healing is reversed. One shared roll for grenade and medical feints. For example, with Chad set to 20% and medical preference 50%, with both types eligible: 10% medical, 10% grenade, 80% no feint. Otherwise the available type is used. Both share the chances, distances and cooldowns below. A protected PMC near a doorway may draw a grenade to bait a nearby known opponent, then put it away without throwing. The opponent is never forced to react. One feint replaces doorway reconnaissance, or is part of an entry already selected by D07. It never chains after a peek. The grenade must exist and be accessible. Cover, actual hands and weapon readiness are checked. Danger cancels the feint, with normal animation time to recover the weapon. RR records requested actions separately from observed hands and perceived reactions.
DoorFakeMedical.Summary: Medical feints start a real item animation, then cancel it when the item is seen in the hands.

DoorFakeGrenade.Title: Doorway feints - D05 / D06
DoorFakeGrenade.Description: Medical feints start a real item animation, then cancel it when the item is seen in the hands. Bleeding, serious injury and real medical decisions take priority. No item is refunded and no healing is reversed. One shared roll for grenade and medical feints. For example, with Chad set to 20% and medical preference 50%, with both types eligible: 10% medical, 10% grenade, 80% no feint. Otherwise the available type is used. Both share the chances, distances and cooldowns below. A protected PMC near a doorway may draw a grenade to bait a nearby known opponent, then put it away without throwing. The opponent is never forced to react. One feint replaces doorway reconnaissance, or is part of an entry already selected by D07. It never chains after a peek. The grenade must exist and be accessible. Cover, actual hands and weapon readiness are checked. Danger cancels the feint, with normal animation time to recover the weapon. RR records requested actions separately from observed hands and perceived reactions.
DoorFakeGrenade.Summary: A PMC can draw a grenade to bait an opponent, then return to its weapon without throwing.

DoorStepPeek.Title: Take another look from the frame - D04
DoorStepPeek.Description: After returning safely from D02, a PMC can take one or two small steps toward the opening, look with its weapon ready and return to the frame. A second peek needs a different safe viewing angle. D03 keeps its own final angle. The original door cooldown still applies. RR records each step, view, return and cancellation; a movement request alone is never shown as a successful peek.
DoorStepPeek.Summary: After returning safely from D02, a PMC can take one or two small steps toward the opening, look with its weapon ready and return to the frame.

DoorRunBy.Title: Run past a doorway - D03
DoorRunBy.Description: Sprint past the opening on the corridor side, slow down beyond the frame, then walk back with the weapon ready to an offset angle. No jump or room entry. Both routes and body clearance are checked before leaving. The return is checked again from the actual arrival. A blocked path, nearby heard threat, visible enemy or combat emergency ends the plan. RR shows the shared roll, alternatives, actual sprint, return and outcome.
DoorRunBy.Summary: Sprint past the opening on the corridor side, slow down beyond the frame, then walk back with the weapon ready to an offset angle.

EnvironmentContext.Title: Read the surroundings - P10
EnvironmentContext.Description: PMCs distinguish the game's indoor indicators from an overhead surface detected locally. A roof alone does not mean a room is enclosed or that a position is safe. This preview records context for future tactics. It does not yet change grenade arcs, forbid indoor movement or reduce hearing. RR shows the sources, sample age and ceiling result alongside the current behavior.
EnvironmentContext.Summary: PMCs distinguish the game's indoor indicators from an overhead surface detected locally.

SearchAbandonment.Title: Finish an empty search - P09
SearchAbandonment.Description: A PMC can stop searching after checking its last known enemy position without finding anyone. It must be close, on the same floor, looking toward the point and have a clear view. A squadmate reaching the point is not enough. The failed search is remembered for 30 s to avoid retrying the exact same old information. Fresh information can restart the search immediately. Native memory may expire sooner; these settings never extend it.
SearchAbandonment.Summary: A PMC can stop searching after checking its last known enemy position without finding anyone.

SilentSearch.Title: Search after silence - P08
SilentSearch.Description: A PMC may investigate the last place it heard an enemy after waiting. This is a new decision opportunity, not an order to rush. SAIN's search permissions, danger and contact expiry still apply. A normal search can start earlier.
SilentSearch.Summary: A PMC may investigate the last place it heard an enemy after waiting.

ImpactReaction.Title: React when hit - P07
ImpactReaction.Description: Source injury handling for registered custom bot roles only (a custom BaseBrain or BrainsToApply entry). A hit can create or refresh the shooter's exact contact and mark the bot under fire. Ordinary roles keep native SAIN hit handling. This exception does not enable COMET tactics for other bot types.
ImpactReaction.Summary: Source injury handling for registered custom bot roles only (a custom BaseBrain or BrainsToApply entry).

CloseDetection.Title: Notice close enemies - P05
CloseDetection.Description: Remove the third-party and unknown-target attention factors within 6 m. Within 3 m, also cap the corrected sight modifier at 1. This runs before SAIN's repeat-contact bonuses; native visibility, darkness, equipment and other perception processing remain. RR distinguishes a modifier change from an actual visual acquisition.
CloseDetection.Summary: Remove the third-party and unknown-target attention factors within 6 m.

FloorHearing.Title: Hearing between floors - P04
FloorHearing.Description: Reduce native hearing range for vertical separation when the listener is under a roof and lacks line of sight. The source uses height bands (2.5 m and 5.5 m by default), not a count of physical floor slabs. Native obstacle and environment attenuation still apply. Player audio and Ghost hearing are unchanged.
FloorHearing.Summary: Reduce native hearing range for vertical separation when the listener is under a roof and lacks line of sight.

Gunfire.Title: Distant gunfire - P03
Gunfire.Description: React to audible shots using the native SAIN personality's nearby distance. Nearby or recent incoming shots keep native handling. Distant shots can prompt a single look or an occasional search, depending on personality. There is no sustained look lock or extra sound-age limit.
Gunfire.Summary: React to audible shots using the native SAIN personality's nearby distance.

QuietApproach.Title: Quiet approach - P02
QuietApproach.Description: During a search or approach, some PMCs stop sprinting and crouch for the last few metres. Visible threats and urgent actions take priority. This does not slow a committed push or ORBIT's ordinary travel. Chance per contact and encounter. The choice stays stable; 0% disables quiet approaches for that personality. Actual sound still depends on the game's movement and surface rules. RR shows the requested pace, applied limits, roll, progress and reasons for stopping.
QuietApproach.Summary: Approach a known contact quietly over the last few metres.

MovementHearing.Title: Hear nearby bots - P01
MovementHearing.Description: PMCs can notice nearby bots before seeing them. SAIN still decides what they hear based on distance, equipment and surroundings. Ghosts stay silent and do not listen. Other bots and human movement sounds keep their normal behavior. RR distinguishes signals queued for SAIN from sounds a PMC actually heard.
MovementHearing.Summary: PMCs can notice nearby bots before seeing them.

Handoff.Title: Hand control back to SAIN - A13
Handoff.Description: If no COMET tactic is usable, SAIN continues its normal decisions. Urgent actions keep priority. This safety fallback is always available. Runtime errors use the C08 recovery settings above. The handoff delay applies to ordinary unavailable tactics. Failed-attempt memory is preserved. RR records why COMET yielded and the next native decision observed, without treating it as a COMET action.
Handoff.Summary: If no COMET tactic is usable, SAIN continues its normal decisions.

Progress.Title: Plan progress - A12
Progress.Description: PMCs can hold an angle or take a detour, but should not wait or retry the same blocked destination forever. Shooting, treatment, reloading, doors and deliberate search pauses do not consume these timers. Failed routes never become usable just because a timer expires. If no safe alternative is available, SAIN keeps control. RR shows pauses, progress, idle holds and retry cooldowns.
Progress.Summary: PMCs can hold an angle or take a detour, but should not wait or retry the same blocked destination forever.

CoverResponse.Title: Fight or take cover - A11
CoverResponse.Description: Favor a nearby protected spot, or keep firing when reaching cover would mean a long exposed crossing. Paths, known threats and the PMC's mobility matter. Low ammunition, serious injuries and urgent SAIN actions keep priority. Travel times are estimates. RR shows travel and exposure estimates, plus why firing or taking cover was preferred.
CoverResponse.Summary: Favor a nearby protected spot, or keep firing when reaching cover would mean a long exposed crossing.

Opportunity.Title: Heard opportunities - A10
Opportunity.Description: A short opening can make a safe push more attractive. The PMC must hear it, react and reach the perceived position in time. Enemy actions are estimated, never read through walls. A heard shot, sprint or grenade preparation cancels the old opening. Low ammunition, injuries, panic, extra known threats and unsafe routes keep priority. RR shows the original cue, time left, travel estimate and refusal reason.
Opportunity.Summary: A short opening can make a safe push more attractive.

Opponent.Title: Opponent assessment - A09
Opponent.Description: PMCs remember weapons and protection they could see. A witnessed impact or a personally heard treatment is only a hint of injury. Unknown equipment stays neutral; hidden changes do not update the estimate. Confidence fades until the memory expires. A shotgun remains dangerous at close range. No other enemy spotted does not mean the target is alone. RR shows the evidence and its effect on each choice.
Opponent.Summary: PMCs remember weapons and protection they could see.

Loadout.Title: Equipment awareness - A08
Loadout.Description: A shotgun and a scoped rifle favor different engagements. Equipment only nudges usable choices: safe routes, urgent actions and your SAIN settings still come first. These distances guide choices. They are not maximum firing ranges or places a bot must reach. A dot alongside a scope keeps the closer-range profile.
Loadout.Summary: A shotgun and a scoped rifle favor different engagements.

ThreatSelection.Title: Target priority - A07
ThreatSelection.Description: PMCs can react to a nearby opponent or a located attacker without constantly switching targets. Only known, dated contacts count. Hearing footsteps alone does not reveal an enemy or authorize shooting. Old evidence gradually loses influence. SAIN keeps urgent actions and shooting rules. RR records target priority separately from the current combat action.
ThreatSelection.Summary: PMCs can react to a nearby opponent or a located attacker without constantly switching targets.

Fear.Title: Fear & panic - A06
Fear.Description: PMCs react to injuries, heavy suppression, known enemy numbers and squad deaths they witness. Fear builds and fades gradually. Panic picks the best usable response without random mistakes; it never makes an unsafe route usable. Base is the calm starting level (0 to 1). Sensitivity scales the extra fear from perceived danger.
Fear.Summary: PMCs react to injuries, heavy suppression, known enemy numbers and squad deaths they witness.

DecisionVariety.Title: Decision variety - A04
DecisionVariety.Description: Sometimes choose a close runner-up instead of always choosing the highest score. Unsafe and unavailable actions stay excluded. Bots keep their plan; they do not roll again every few seconds. Personality still shapes the choices. Urgent situations use the best available response. Brief sight loss keeps the existing plan without another roll.
DecisionVariety.Summary: Let PMCs choose among similarly useful tactics instead of always taking the highest score.

TacticalMistakes.Title: Occasional mistakes - A05
TacticalMistakes.Description: Rarely choose a less favorable but still usable action. This only happens when decision variety kept the best option. Urgent actions, healing and reloading are not delayed. These chances apply once to a new eligible decision, not each frame. A bot needs a plausible alternative outside the normal variety range, so its overall mistake rate will be lower.
TacticalMistakes.Summary: Allow occasional imperfect choices when a safe alternative exists.

VisibleCombat.Title: Visible enemy - A02
VisibleCombat.Description: Shoot, take cover or push. Only usable choices compete. Zero disables a choice; weights are preferences, not percentages. Exact enemy health stays unknown. A09 can use dated observations of visible equipment. Other threats count only if the bot has seen, heard or received their position.

SightContinuity.Title: Brief sight loss - A03
SightContinuity.Description: Keep watching the last seen spot when an enemy briefly disappears behind a door or corner. During this hold, bots do not track hidden movement or fire blindly. New threats, hits and urgent actions interrupt the hold. Once the timer ends, lost-contact decisions take over.
SightContinuity.Summary: Keep watching the last seen spot when an enemy briefly disappears behind a door or corner.

PostCombat.Title: Recover after a fight - H04
PostCombat.Description: After a real fight ends, PMCs take cover, treat useful injuries, top up their magazine and watch briefly. They may rejoin their leader or check the last known enemy position. A hidden but still known enemy keeps normal combat active. Finished work releases control to normal behavior, including ORBIT when installed. Medical choices use H01; interruption and posture protections use H02/H03 when enabled. Time limits never cut a medicine animation. Unusable supplies and failed routes do not cause endless retries. A new threat returns control to combat. One roll per fight, reduced to one fifth below 40% health. This is a short security check, not a loot objective.
PostCombat.Summary: After a real fight ends, PMCs take cover, treat useful injuries, top up their magazine and watch briefly.

General.Title: General
General.Description: COMET affects PMC bots and AI Player Scavs only. Human players, ordinary scavs and bosses are excluded. SAIN keeps its own settings.
General.Summary: Enable or disable COMET tactics for PMCs and AI Player Scavs.

LostContact.Title: Lost contact - A01
LostContact.Description: Preferences and limits for acting on a recent known contact. Zero disables a preference.
LostContact.Summary: Preferences and limits for acting on a recent known contact.

Aggression.Title: Personality tactics
Aggression.Description: How each assigned personality approaches a fight. This does not assign personalities or change SAIN settings.
Aggression.Summary: How each assigned personality approaches a fight.

Logging.Title: Logging
Logging.Description: Choose how much COMET writes to its local diagnostic files. Raid Review still receives the same decisions, observations and raid summaries. Changes apply next raid.
Logging.Summary: Reduce detailed files without hiding anything from Raid Review.

TacticCounters.Title: Decision counters - T02
TacticCounters.Description: Build a compact raid report from existing events in the background. Counts do not change decisions or consume randomness. Exact opportunities are currently identified for A01/A02 choices, A04/A05 draws and D05/D06 feints. Other features report event coverage only; missing measurements are never treated as zero attempts. A command accepted by SAIN is not proof of execution. Changes apply next raid.
TacticCounters.Summary: Compare eligible opportunities, draws and observed execution.

CombatJournal.Title: Combat journal - T01
CombatJournal.Description: Record actual PMC actions, known contacts, locally observed damage and confirmed deaths. Raid Review groups these observations by PMC and action. This is diagnostic correlation, not proof that a tactic caused a kill or death. Remote Fika player damage may be missing from the host; downed players are not confirmed deaths.
CombatJournal.Summary: Record actual PMC actions, known contacts, locally observed damage and confirmed deaths.

WeaponJournal.Title: Weapon changes and loops - T03
WeaponJournal.Description: Observe requests, actual weapons in hands and readiness. Repeated reversals are grouped into possible-loop incidents. Empty or broken weapons, range changes and medical/grenade returns can explain legitimate changes. No cancellation or gameplay effect.
WeaponJournal.Summary: Observe requests, actual weapons in hands and readiness.

ControlJournal.Title: Control transitions - T04
ControlJournal.Description: Observe actual layers and COMET execution separately. Explain medical/reload/recovery waits where observed; unknown reasons stay unknown. Group repeated rapid returns without delaying combat. Idle does not mean stuck. Existing ORBIT/QB delays stay unchanged. Settings apply next raid.
ControlJournal.Summary: Read-only handoff diagnostics and raid report in RR.

Performance.Title: Performance capture
Performance.Description: Temporarily record COMET timings, managed allocations and slow frames during normal play. Reports are saved on the machine running the game in BepInEx/COMET/performance. The next raid uses these settings. This adds measurement overhead; switch it off after testing. It does not replace a GPU or whole-game profiler.
Performance.Summary: Find costly COMET features and correlate them with stutters.

CoverScan.Enabled.Label: Keep cover results stable between frames

DoorClosing.OpenGrace.Label: Protect doors opened by the squad

DoorClosing.OccupiedRadius.Label: Keep doorway clear of other actors

DoorMotion.PushAway.Label: Push doors away from the bot

SquadManeuver.Chance.Label: Chance to start a squad maneuver
SquadManeuver.Chance.Help: Chance to propose a coordinated maneuver when the enemy is hidden and squad support is available. Higher values make eligible proposals more frequent; they do not guarantee a flank.

SquadManeuver.RearWatch.Label: Watch a known rear threat when another supporter is available

RestLights.Enabled.Label: Switch off accessories during quiet pauses

SquadVoice.Mode.Label: Squad communication mode
SquadVoice.Mode.Help: Normal keeps SAIN's squad callouts. Disabled mutes them, including grenade alerts, as in the source default.

SquadFire.ClearDelay.Label: Keep the lane clear before releasing

FireLane.Width.Label: Margin on each side of the firing axis

FireLane.Retry.Label: Retry after giving way to native movement

SquadStorm.Enabled.Label: Enable coordinated assaults
SquadStorm.Enabled.Help: Let nearby squadmates prepare an assault together when personally observed weakness or a heard opening justifies it. Each attacker still needs a safe route and must be ready.

SquadStorm.Weakness.Label: Required perceived weakness
SquadStorm.Weakness.Help: Minimum weakness inferred from personal observations or heard openings. A higher threshold requires stronger evidence before proposing an assault.

Crossfire.ContactAge.Label: Maximum information age
Crossfire.ContactAge.Help: Maximum age to start an angle change. A validated route may finish while it keeps making progress, within its original movement timeout. Reaching the point does not refresh enemy information.

Crossfire.OutdoorAngle.Label: Preferred outdoor angle
Crossfire.OutdoorAngle.Help: Target separation from the supporting teammate's angle. For distant enemies, COMET scales this to the local movement radius while still requiring at least 10 degrees of improvement.

Crossfire.IndoorAngle.Label: Preferred indoor angle
Crossfire.IndoorAngle.Help: Target separation indoors. Scales to the reachable local angle for distant enemies, with at least 10 degrees of improvement. Door, cover and teammate safety checks still apply.

ReadyStance.CueFreshness.Label: Maximum age of a new nearby clue

MedicalPosture.ResumeDelay.Label: Stable weapon and posture before tactics resume

SurgeryInterruption.Enabled.Label: Enable surgery interruption
SurgeryInterruption.Enabled.Help: Cancel ongoing COMET-selected surgery when a hit, dangerous grenade or nearby known threat makes it unsafe. Putting the kit away still takes time. Requires medical choices.

MedicalChoice.Enabled.Label: Enable medical choices
MedicalChoice.Enabled.Help: Let COMET choose first aid, a useful stim, surgery or waiting. Urgent bleeding and vital injuries come first. It uses the medicines the PMC actually carries.

MedicalChoice.HitDelay.Label: Ordinary treatment delay after a hit

MedicalChoice.EmergencyStimDelay.Label: Emergency treatment delay after a hit

MedicalChoice.StimHealth.Label: Health fraction to prefer a useful stim
MedicalChoice.StimHealth.Help: Health fraction below which a useful carried stim can be preferred. Vital injuries can also justify one. 0.35 means 35% health.
MedicalChoice.StimHealth.Example: 0.35 is 35% of maximum health. It is a health threshold, not a 35% chance to use a stim.

MedicalChoice.SurgeryDistance.Label: Minimum known threat distance for surgery

MedicalChoice.RetryDelay.Label: Delay after a failed or ended treatment

GasExposure.Enabled.Label: React to Manimal CS gas when available

GrenadeFilter.AllowFlash.Label: Allow offensive flash grenades
GrenadeFilter.AllowFlash.Help: Allow a carried flash grenade for an offensive throw. It still needs a safe trajectory and the usual throw permissions. This does not enable gas or smoke attacks.

GrenadeTrajectory.DoorDepthFirst.Label: First point behind an open door

GrenadeTrajectory.DoorDepthSecond.Label: Second point behind an open door

GrenadeTrajectory.DoorDepthThird.Label: Third point behind an open door

GrenadeJudgment.BaseChance.Label: Base chance
GrenadeJudgment.BaseChance.Help: Starting chance for a worthwhile, safe grenade attempt. The bonuses and penalties below adjust it. Increasing this makes eligible throws more likely, without bypassing safety.
GrenadeJudgment.BaseChance.Example: A base chance of 20% plus a 15-point situational bonus makes 35% before other bonuses or penalties. An unsafe trajectory still prevents the throw.

HandsRecovery.ReloadStaleSeconds.Label: Confirm stale weapon state for
HandsRecovery.ReloadStaleSeconds.Help: Continuous inactivity before repairing a stale reload or switch flag. A missing reload idle notification always requires at least 16 seconds, an inserted magazine and an idle animation.

ShotGeometry.AllowPenetration.Label: Allow plausible penetration through other surfaces using native data

WeaponRange.LostContactSeconds.Label: Keep long-range choice after losing contacts

QuickReload.RecoverDroppedMagazine.Label: Recover dropped magazines after combat
QuickReload.RecoverDroppedMagazine.Help: After an emergency reload, return for the discarded magazine when the fight is over. Keeps its remaining ammunition. Combat interrupts recovery; blocked or unavailable magazines are left behind.

WeaponReturn.MinimumHold.Label: Minimum time with a ready weapon

WeaponReturn.DistanceMargin.Label: Extra distance beyond the pistol range

WeaponReturn.PistolReturnDelay.Label: Give the primary time to reload

ReloadTiming.LostContactDelay.Label: Expect a repeek after sight loss

CoverTravel.Enabled.Label: Keep a ready weapon facing a nearby threat when walking to cover

AdsTravel.Enabled.Label: Release the sights during non-firing tactical movement

CoverFeint.Jump.Label: Allow a safe jump on the first peek and return

CoverFeint.PeekChance.Label: Bait peek chance
CoverFeint.PeekChance.Help: Chance for a healthy, aggressive PMC outdoors to bait a known opponent with a peek. It needs a safe return route. Increasing this allows more attempts, not longer exposure.
CoverFeint.PeekChance.Example: At 25%, roughly one in four eligible attempts passes this roll over many attempts. A single raid can differ, and missing cover prevents the attempt before it rolls.

OutdoorRelocation.Enabled.Label: Reposition outdoors after being engaged first

OutdoorRelocation.Grenade.Label: Allow an optional grenade before moving

OutdoorRelocation.RetryDelay.Label: Minimum delay before a new opportunity

TacticalJump.AirShotChance.Label: Air firing chance
TacticalJump.AirShotChance.Help: Each PMC rolls once per opponent for permission to shoot while airborne. Increasing this allows more PMCs to try; SAIN's aiming and firing checks still decide whether a shot happens.

HoldAngle.Enabled.Label: Correct a blocked angle during a COMET Hold

HoldAngle.AdjustPose.Label: Allow a higher posture when safe

HoldAngle.MaxStep.Label: Maximum step from the original position

Enabled.Label: Enable COMET
Enabled.Help: Apply COMET tactics to PMCs and AI Player Scavs. Changes apply next raid.

MovementHearing.RangeMultiplier.Label: Added sound range multiplier
MovementHearing.RangeMultiplier.Help: Multiplies SAIN's ranges for the additional movement sounds. Higher values let those sounds be heard farther away. A noise does not reveal a target or authorize firing.
MovementHearing.RangeMultiplier.Example: With a sound range of 40 m, a multiplier of 0.5 gives 20 m before other hearing checks.

QuietApproach.Enabled.Label: Let PMCs approach known contacts quietly
QuietApproach.Enabled.Help: Let eligible PMCs slow down near a last known position. Personality chances decide who tries it. Visible danger, urgent actions and ordinary ORBIT travel keep priority.

QuietApproach.WalkDistance.Label: Stop sprinting within
QuietApproach.WalkDistance.Help: Stop sprinting when the checked path to the last known position is within this distance. Higher values start the quiet approach sooner.

QuietApproach.CrouchDistance.Label: Crouch within
QuietApproach.CrouchDistance.Help: Crouch within this much checked path distance. This uses the last known position, not the enemy's hidden live position.

QuietApproach.CrouchExitMargin.Label: Crouch exit margin
QuietApproach.CrouchExitMargin.Help: Extra path distance before returning to the faster pace. A larger gap prevents repeated pace changes near a threshold.

QuietApproach.Budget.Label: Quiet approach time budget
QuietApproach.Budget.Help: Maximum quiet approach time shared across targets in the encounter. Higher values allow a longer slow approach.

QuietApproach.FireDelay.Label: Wait after incoming fire
QuietApproach.FireDelay.Help: Maximum time allowed for this stage. Fresh danger interrupts immediately.

Gunfire.InterestDistance.Label: Maximum distant interest

Gunfire.LookDuration.Label: Look duration

Gunfire.LookInterval.Help: Minimum interval between one-shot look commands. No sustained steering lock.

Notes.Title: Official SAIN integration - I01
Notes.Description: Always active. COMET checks both official SAIN 4.5.1 files and its installed hooks at startup. A failed check leaves COMET inactive and records the failing stage. Your SAIN preset stays unchanged. The startup report above is not a live connection monitor or proof of successful combat. Decisions requested, accepted, refused and interrupted remain visible in logs and Raid Review.

Notes.Title: Correct SAIN preset - C14
Notes.Description: Always active. COMET reads the SAIN preset you selected, even if SAIN loads another preset for its editor. Selecting a different SAIN preset takes effect immediately for these reads. Your COMET settings stay fixed for the current raid; server edits apply next raid. Missing SAIN settings cannot enable an action. Logs and Raid Review show the selected preset and COMET revision when this context changes. This protects COMET's reads without changing SAIN's global settings or other bots.

Notes.Title: End-of-raid cleanup - C13
Notes.Description: Always active, including when combat features are disabled. COMET releases its bot actions, cover searches, door operations, event subscriptions and raid caches. Each cleanup step runs independently, so one failure cannot skip the rest. Old server responses cannot configure a later raid. Each Fika machine clears its own transport queues. Logs and Raid Review include a cleanup report with released bot counts, duration and any failures. No forced garbage collection or changes to corpses.

Notes.Title: Invalid movement and references - C10
Notes.Description: Always active while COMET is enabled. Refuse movement commands for dead, downed or invalid PMCs. Ignore destroyed player references and outdated removal events. A shot or grenade from a dead shooter still causes damage; only an unsafe reaction to a destroyed source is skipped. Valid revives can move again. Only the AI authority applies these guards in Fika. Logs and Raid Review show blocked calls and grouped repeat counts.

Notes.Title: Death and revive safety - C09
Notes.Description: Always active. COMET stops its actions when a PMC dies or is downed. Each module is cleaned independently. An eligible revived PMC starts with fresh decisions; old actions cannot resume. Failed cleanup keeps COMET disabled for that bot. Logs and Raid Review record these transitions. This does not create corpses or change Fika's revive rules.

Notes.Title: Understand the choices
Notes.Description: COMET records choices, scores, selection probabilities, known contacts and route risks in BepInEx/COMET/diagnostics. The COMET branch of Raid Review shows them in the behavior page and on map hover, including why a plan was kept or interrupted. A choice accepted by SAIN does not prove that the action succeeded.
